title: Odd-token latency investigation: flash attn + paged-KV + cont-batching
content:
Summary:

Short version: after landing combined changes for FlashAttention v2 + paged-KV memory spill + continuous-batching coalescer (PR 2798), our canary workloads show a small class of requests with elevated token latency and increased token-drop (small growth in early-stopping). This doc describes the investigation, the eval sweep across prompt sets, observed diffs, hypotheses, and next steps.

Why it matters:
- These are low-frequency but high-impact: tail latency spikes at token boundaries cause downstream user-visible pauses and a measurable uptick in cost due to wasted partial tokens on retries.
- Root of issue appears when flash-attn micro-kernel interacts with paged-KV page boundaries under continuous batching where request coalescing reorders micro-batches.

Timeline (brief):
- 2026-03-02: Kernel patch series submitted (flash attn micro-optimizations + paged-KV page-pinning)
- 2026-03-04: Continuous-batching coalescer merged to reduce small-request overheads
- 2026-03-09: Shadow canary rollout to 10% traffic for dev-1 region; alerts for token-latency surfaced
- 2026-03-10: Initial triage by applied-ml; reproduced in lab on synthetic replay
- 2026-03-11: Large eval sweep launched across 6 prompt sets (below)
- 2026-03-12: First draft of analysis (this doc)

Datasets & prompt sets used (short names):
- short-instr (5000 prompts) — single-shot instructions, <128 tokens target
- codegen-sm (1k prompts) — short code completion patterns, sensitive to exact token alignment
- long-summarize (2k prompts) — 2k-6k token context summarization, exercises KV paging heavily
- convo-multi (3k prompts) — multi-turn chat sims, typical of hosted chat use-case
- perf-edge (synthetic 1k) — intentionally crafted sequences that trigger page boundary tokens (odd token lengths)
- eval-regression-set (250 prompts) — benchmark of golden outputs for quality checks

Baseline vs candidate kernels:
- Baseline: runtime v1.48 with legacy attention, contiguous-KV (no paging), batching disabled for microbench (older coalescer)
- Candidate: runtime v1.51 with FlashAttention v2 microkernel, paged-KV enabled, continuous-batching coalescer enabled (PR 2798 meta-combo)

Eval methodology:
- Replay harness: deterministic replay of production traces and the 6 prompt sets into isolated canary GPU pool (same seed for randomness where applicable).
- Metrics captured at token granularity: token_latency_ms, p50/p95/p99, token_throughput, generation_steps_taken, early_stops, avg_logprob, perplexity, exact-match for codegen snippets, rouge-L for summarization.
- Per-request traces collected for any request with token_latency_ms > p95_baseline * 1.5 or generation_steps deviating by > 5 tokens from baseline.
- Statistical test: two-sided paired t-test on per-prompt token-latency; bootstrapped CI for small-sample quality metrics.

Key results (high level):
- Overall token-throughput: +3.8% (candidate faster on average)
- Mean token latency: -2.1% (candidate slightly faster)
- p95 token latency: +12.4% (candidate worse — spike behavior)
- p99 token latency: +28.6% (candidate worse on tails)
- Early stop rate (generation truncated due to internal guard): baseline 0.41% -> candidate 0.72% (delta +0.31pp)
- Codegen exact-match: baseline 72.6% -> candidate 71.9% (non-significant, p=0.14)
- Summarization rouge-L: baseline 0.421 -> candidate 0.418 (bootstrapped 95% CI overlap)

Where the regression concentrates:
- perf-edge and long-summarize sets show the largest p95/p99 increases.
- Short-instr and convo-multi show marginal tail regressions but no quality loss.
- Failures correlate strongly with sequences that hit paged-KV boundary right after a long attention window (i.e., final chunk token aligns to page boundary).

Trace examples (anonymized):
- Trace A (long-summarize): observed a sequence of tokens where token N has latency 4.2x baseline; backend trace shows extra paged-KV synchronous page fetch blocking microkernel warps for ~30ms.
- Trace B (perf-edge): coalescer merged 3 separate short requests into a micro-batch; flash-attn kernel assumes contiguous KV offsets and does a KV-index shift that results in an extra memcpy for the first token of request-2 (contention with page eviction path).

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Paged-KV page boundary synchronous fetches are not fully asynchronous in the new paged-KV path when combined with the micro-batched scheduling used by continuous-batching; this creates head-of-line blocking on rare sequences. (High confidence)
2) FlashAttention v2 microkernel expects buffer alignment that can be violated when the coalescer reorders micro-batches; in some alignment cases we pay an extra memcpy and kernel fallback that increases per-token latency. (Medium confidence)
3) Timing window regression: continuous-batching introduced slightly longer tail for small coalesced bursts leading to rebuffering and triggering early-stop heuristics on marginal generations. (Low-medium confidence)

Evidence for hypothesis 1:
- Instrumented page-fetch histogram shows a small hump around 12–35ms for candidate; baseline has near-zero for same requests.
- Heap/VM stats in trace show page pinned then a synchronous read from device visible in scheduler timeline.

Evidence for hypothesis 2:
- Kernel logs show a fallback path executed in 0.6% of micro-batches; correlates with coalescer-reorder markers.
- Reproducing with coalescer disabled eliminates the kernel fallback occurrences.

Root cause synthesis (working):
- Interaction syndrome: paged-KV synchronous fallback + kernel alignment fallback + request coalescing -> rare path where a request waits on two dependent synchronous operations causing a multiplicative tail increase. Not a single change regression but emergent when three changes are composed.

Short-term mitigations applied in lab:
- Disable paging on canary pool (rollback paged-KV flag) -> tail latency returns to baseline quickly.
- Apply coalescer config change (max-coalesce=1 for small-requests) -> kernel fallback events disappear in lab.
- Hotfix PR drafted to make paged-KV fetch asynchronous (ENG-INF-4821); currently in code review.

Recommended route forward (prod-safe):
1) Immediate: revert paged-KV enablement in the canary rollout for region dev-1 (rollback staged 2026-03-12 18:00 UTC).
2) Short term (2 weeks): ship coalescer conservative config for small requests, merge asynchronous paged fetch change, add kernel alignment assertion in debug builds.
3) Medium term (4–8 weeks): add end-to-end integration tests that exercise combination of: paged-KV boundary conditions + micro-batching reorders + flash-attn kernel alignment scenarios. Add synthetic perf-edge tests to CI with low-frequency triggers to catch this emergent behavior earlier.
4) Long term (Q3): revisit KV page-sizing heuristics and scheduler heuristics to avoid head-of-line blocking; consider proactive prefetch for anticipated page transitions in long-context workloads.

Action items (owners):
- Maya: coordinate rollback and update canary traffic config (done 2026-03-12) — jira ENG-INF-4825
- Devon: finish async paged-fetch patch and open PR for review (target 2026-03-16)
- Ethan: instrument additional trace points in runtime to capture ordering keys for coalescer decisions (target 2026-03-15)
- Sara: expand eval-regression-set with 500 more perf-edge prompts mimicking page boundary tokens (target 2026-03-18)
- QA: run end-to-end canary smoke after each incremental change (checklists attached in linked confluence page)

Open questions / notes to self:
- How often do production workloads hit the pathological alignment? Current estimate from sampled traces: ~0.08% of requests; peak in some tenants up to 0.6% due to long-context summarizers.
- Cost impact: measured retries + partial token waste -> estimated $0.002 per 10k requests at current mix (small). But brand/latency impact is larger.
- Do we need a rollout gate for multi-change kernel + scheduler combos? Proposal: require combo shadow-eval for any merge that touches kernel + KV + batching heuristics simultaneously.

Appendix A — quick numeric table (per-prompt-set p95 delta candidate vs baseline):
- short-instr: +6%
- codegen-sm: +4%
- long-summarize: +28%
- convo-multi: +9%
- perf-edge: +62%
- eval-regression-set: +3%

Appendix B — reproduction recipe (lab):
1) checkout runtime@v1.51-candidate (PR 2798 combined)
2) launch 2x A100 canary pool with paged-KV and coalescer enabled
3) run replay harness with perf-edge + long-summarize sets at 100rps for 30m
4) collect per-token traces, filter for p95>baseline*1.5 and inspect page-fetch histogram

Appendix C — immediate communication (internal):
- Posted summary to #applied-ml and #runtime-ops on 2026-03-12 with mitigations and rollback plan.
- Product/CS notified for potential customer-facing blips; hold on public incident announcement until we confirm impact scope.

Short raw notes (brain-dump):
- weird alignment: page boundary + coalescer re-order = memcpy path taken
- need to confirm if flash-attn fallback actually does more work or just stalls waiting on lock
- test idea: add randomized shift to micro-batch offsets in unit test to surface alignment issues early
- add a small perf test that simulates 3x coalesced requests where second request starts at offset X (page-1 boundary)

If you want me to convert this to a slide deck for ENG leadership or a one-pager for CS, ping and I’ll draft.

-- Maya
